Burstiness. How much your sentence lengths vary. Low means every sentence is about the same length. High mixes long sentences with short ones. Try it: raise it if the text reads like a drumbeat.

Interleave. Whether long and short sentences take turns. Below zero they alternate. Above zero, long ones bunch together, and so do short ones. Try it: pull it below zero for a steadier back and forth.
Length. The average sentence length you are aiming for, in words. Lexiphon splits or joins sentences to get near it. Try it: a low number for brisk copy, a high one for a slower read.
End weight. How many sentences should finish on a word that carries meaning, such as a noun or a verb, and not on a small word like “it” or “of”. Try it: raise it to make endings land harder.
Tempo. How fast the tune plays, in beats per minute. It also sets the spacing of the echo.
Key. The note the melody is built on. It also retunes the looping backdrop to match.
Glide. How smoothly one note slides into the next. At 0 each note steps cleanly. Higher values slur them together. Try it: around 100 for a singing slide.
Cutoff. How bright the sound is. Turn it down for a darker, softer tone and up for a sharper, brighter one. Try it: turn it as the tune plays.
Emphasis. How strongly the filter boosts the sound right at the cutoff. Higher values give a more nasal, singing edge.
Contour. How far the brightness opens at the start of each note before it settles. Higher values give a sharper pluck.
Space. How much echo and room sound surrounds the notes.
Bed. The volume of the looping backdrop that belongs to each voice you chose. Try it: turn it up for atmosphere, down for the bare tune.
Volume. The overall loudness.

Play. Plays your output text as a tune. Longer words play higher notes, small words play softly, and a sentence that ends on a strong word finishes on a high note.
Loop. Repeats the tune until you press Stop, so you can keep turning dials and hear what each one does.
Sound. Switches all sound on or off. Nothing plays until you press Play or a key.
Pitch wheel. Bends the pitch up or down for as long as you hold it. It springs back when you let go.
Mod wheel. Adds a gentle wobble to the pitch and a slow sweep to the brightness. It stays where you leave it.
Keyboard. Play it with the mouse or your finger, or use the A to semicolon keys on a computer keyboard. Z and X move down and up an octave.
Scope. Each dot is one sentence, and higher means longer. The dashed line is your Length target. Red dots end on a small word, and the white line follows the sound as it plays.
Use as input. Moves the rewritten text into the box, so the dials work from this version.
